ABSTRACT

AN ASSESSMENT OF WATER QUALITY IN THIRIRIKA RIVER, KIAMBU COUNTY, KENYA

Journal: Journal CleanWAS (JCleanWAS)

Author: Justine Bundi, Joan Nyika, Ednah Onyari

This is an open access article distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License CC BY 4.0, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited

Doi: 10.26480/jcleanwas.01.26.63.67

In the contemporary society, advances to urbanization and industrialization is triggering surface water pollution, rendering the resource unfit for human consumption. Such trends have serious ramifications to public and environmental health despite the fact that such studies are limited in Kenya and Sub-Saharan Africa at large. The current study seeks to close the gap by evaluating the impact of human activities on the spatial water quality of in Thiririka river of Kiambu county, using a quantitative study. Water samples were collected in upstream, midstream and downstream sections of the river before being analyzed in situ and in the laboratory for comparison with the national environmental management authority (NEMA) predefined standards. The water quality index (WQI) was computed using the weighted arithmetic method thereafter. Pollution was minimal upstream and most of the assayed parameters were within the predefined standards. Midstream and downstream sections of the river showed increased pollution levels and nitrates, ammonium, BOD5, and COD exceeded the NEMA water quality standards. The WQI had excellent water upstream with exception of January unlike downstream sections where levels ranged from 218 to 315, which was water unfit for consumption. In January 2025, reduced dilution effect and low pollutant flushing was attributable to the high concentrations of physicochemical parameters and high WQI levels. Human activities were associated to pollution in the river and as such, conservation and intervention measures should be prioritized.
